artworks.title: Apollo and Diana Attacking the Children of Niobe
artworks.description: David's Rome prize canvas — Apollo and Diana raining arrows on Niobe's children, the Metamorphoses slaughter as neoclassical terror.

artworks.title: Apollo and Diana Kill the Children of Niobe
artworks.description: Boeckhorst's Baroque massacre — the twins' wrath among the Niobids, maternal boast answered in blood.

artworks.title: The Florentine Niobids
artworks.description: The Florentine Niobids — Roman marble group that taught Europe the myth as sculpture: children dying, mother already turning to stone.

artworks.title: The Children of Niobe Killed by Apollo and Diana
artworks.description: Jombert's Prix de Rome — the Niobids falling under Apollo and Diana, Leto's insult paid in a mother's emptied arms.

popCulture.title: Niobe
popCulture.description: The slaughter of the Niobids remains the myth of maternal boast answered by arrows — grief petrified on Sipylus.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book 6 — Niobe's boast against Leto and the slaughter of her children: the source that petrifies her tears on Sipylus.
